ideas.title: Settler-Style Resource Bank Tray with Longest-Road/Largest-Army Dials
ideas.concept: A 5-compartment resource cube/card tray shaped like a wooden trading post, with two integrated rotating dial trackers on the short end (for the two 'special card' bonuses) so players stop losing the cardboard tokens.
ideas.rationale: Catan remains the best-selling modern family board game worldwide (Spin Master/Catan Studio reports it as a perennial top-3 seller), and 'Catan organizer' is one of the most searched terms on Etsy/Printables board-game accessory storefronts, showing sustained aftermarket accessory demand for this specific title.
ideas.differentiation: Most existing Catan organizers on Printables/Thingiverse are flat card-and-cube trays; none combine the resource bank with functional rotating bonus-card dials, removing two of the most commonly lost small cardboard pieces in the base game.
ideas.producibility_notes: 3 printed parts: base tray, and two identical dial assemblies (dial + friction-fit axle post molded into tray, no separate hardware). No features under 1mm; dial needs 0.2-0.3mm clearance for smooth rotation. Single color per part is fine; two-tone (tray + dials) recommended for visual pop but not required.
ideas.margin_case: Approx. 5hr print, ~180g PLA at $0.03/g material (~$5.40 cost) plus ~30 min labor equivalent; sell at $28. A hobbyist who already owns a $50+ game will pay a modest accessory upcharge to fix a well-known annoyance (lost bonus cards), giving healthy margin room.
ideas.prompt: Concept: A tabletop resource-and-bonus-card organizer tray for a settlement-trading board game. It has 5 rectangular compartments sized for stacks of small resource cards or wooden resource cubes, plus two rotating dial trackers set into circular recesses at one short end of the tray, each dial showing a printed/engraved number scale 2-10 that the player spins to remember which bonus card they hold. Purpose: keeps a family board game's resource cards organized during play and prevents loss of the two special achievement cards, for board-game hobbyists and gift buyers. Style: warm wood-cabin aesthetic, beveled edges, subtle plank-texture surface, natural wood-tone or dark-walnut single color, minimal ornamentation beyond the plank texture. Technical specification: overall tray footprint approximately 220mm x 90mm x 25mm tall; 3 total parts (1 tray body with two integrated cylindrical dial posts printed in place, 2 separate dial discs 30mm diameter x 4mm thick); FDM PLA material; dial-to-post clearance 0.25mm for free rotation without wobble; dial post diameter 6mm, dial center bore 6.25mm; card compartments each 65mm x 45mm x 20mm deep with a 2mm radius on all interior corners for easy card pickup; minimum wall thickness 2mm throughout; no assembly hardware, dials snap over posts by hand and are retained by a 0.5mm friction lip at the post tip.

ideas.title: Birdhouse Nest Sorter for Wingspan Egg & Food Tokens
ideas.concept: A stackable pair of trays styled as a birdhouse: the top tray has 5 round 'nest' wells sized for egg meeples, and the bottom tray has 5 wells sized for food tokens, with a hinged roof lid that closes over both.
ideas.rationale: Wingspan has stayed in BoardGameGeek's overall top-100 ranked games for multiple years running and is frequently cited as the modern gateway game most associated with heavy aftermarket accessory purchasing (egg-meeple upgrades, food-token upgrades) on BGG marketplace and Etsy, showing buyers already spend extra on this specific title's components.
ideas.differentiation: Existing Wingspan inserts on Printables focus on box-interior card/board storage; this is a standalone on-table sorting caddy shaped like a birdhouse (thematically tied to the game) rather than a generic divided box, with a closable roof lid so unused tokens travel without spilling.
ideas.producibility_notes: 3 printed parts: bottom food tray, top egg tray, roof lid. Lid attaches via a simple friction-fit peg hinge (2x 3mm pegs into 3.2mm sockets, no metal hardware). No sub-1mm features. Recommended 2-color print (tan body + brown roof) but a single-color version is producible.
ideas.margin_case: Approx. 4.5hr print, ~150g PLA (~$4.50 material cost); sell at $24. Wingspan players already routinely buy upgrade sets for eggs/food (a known behavior in this fanbase), so a themed organizer at this price is a plausible impulse add-on for a $60 game.
ideas.prompt: Concept: A stackable two-tier sorting caddy shaped like a small birdhouse for a nature-themed card game's egg and food tokens. The bottom tier is a tray with 5 round wells (for food tokens/dice) arranged in a row, the top tier is a tray with 5 shallower round wells (for egg-shaped meeples) that sits on top and locks in place via 4 small alignment pegs, and a peaked triangular roof piece hinges open on 2 friction-fit pegs to cover both trays when not in play. Purpose: keeps small egg and food tokens sorted and contained during a bird-collection board game session and while transporting the box, for board-game hobbyists and gift buyers. Style: whimsical birdhouse exterior with a round entry-hole cutout on one end purely decorative, smooth rounded roof ridge, light tan body with a contrasting brown roof, low ornamentation otherwise. Technical specification: overall assembled footprint approximately 160mm x 90mm x 70mm tall (roof closed); 3 parts total: bottom tray (160x90x25mm) with 5 round wells 22mm diameter x 15mm deep, top tray (160x90x20mm) with 5 round wells 16mm diameter x 10mm deep plus 4 downward alignment pegs 4mm diameter x 3mm tall matching 4.3mm sockets in the bottom tray rim, and a roof lid (170x95x35mm peaked) with 2 hinge pegs 3mm diameter x 4mm long fitting into 3.2mm diameter sockets molded into the top tray's short ends; suggested dual-color FDM PLA (single-color acceptable fallback); minimum wall thickness 2mm; hinge pegs need 0.2mm clearance for rotation without breaking; all well corners radiused 1.5mm for easy token removal.

ideas.title: Catapult-Trigger Castle Dice Tower
ideas.concept: A turreted castle-shaped dice tower where dice are loaded into a top hopper, and pulling a small lever arm fires a spring-free catapult paddle (driven by a printed torsion mechanism) that flings the dice down through the internal baffle chute into a moat-shaped catch tray.
ideas.rationale: 'Kinetic' and 'mechanism' dice towers (as opposed to static funnel towers) are a consistently top-selling sub-category on Etsy's tabletop-accessory storefronts and are frequently featured in Reddit r/3Dprinting and r/boardgames 'cool prints' threads, showing buyers pay a premium over plain funnel towers specifically for the moving-part novelty.
ideas.differentiation: The vast majority of printed dice towers on Printables/Thingiverse are static gravity funnels; this one adds a working catapult-trigger mechanism using only printed parts (no springs/screws), turning dice-rolling itself into a mini-game moment rather than just a randomizer.
ideas.producibility_notes: 5 printed parts: tower body (2 halves that slot together), catapult paddle arm, printed-flexure torsion hinge pin, lever trigger, moat catch tray. Requires a live-hinge flexure detail approx 0.8mm thick that must be called out explicitly for the printer to get right (too thick = won't flex, too thin = snaps). No metal hardware; assembly is press-fit only.
ideas.margin_case: Approx. 9hr print, ~320g PLA (~$9.60 material cost) due to the tower height and mechanism; sell at $42. Novelty/kinetic dice towers with a working mechanism regularly sell in the $35-55 range on Etsy, well above plain funnel towers ($15-20), because the moving-part gimmick is the entire value proposition.
ideas.prompt: Concept: A castle-turret-shaped dice tower with an internal catapult firing mechanism. Dice are dropped into a hopper opening at the top of the tower, and pulling an external lever arm on the tower's side rotates a paddle (mounted on a printed flexure torsion hinge) that flicks the dice sideways into an internal zigzag baffle chute, which channels them down and out through an arched doorway at the base into a moat-shaped catch tray that surrounds the tower's footprint. Purpose: a tabletop dice-rolling accessory for board-game and tabletop-RPG players who want a fun, noisy, mechanical way to randomize dice rolls instead of a plain funnel tower, primarily a gift/novelty purchase. Style: medieval castle turret with crenellated battlements at the top, arched stone-block texture on the exterior walls, stone-grey single color (or grey walls with a contrasting wood-brown lever and paddle), light ornamentation limited to the battlement and arch details. Technical specification: overall footprint approximately 90mm x 90mm base, tower height 180mm, moat catch tray outer diameter 160mm; 5 parts total: two tower body half-shells that press-fit together with 4 integrated 3mm alignment pins, one catapult paddle arm (60mm long), one flexure hinge pin connecting the paddle to the lever with a living-hinge flex section 0.8mm thick x 10mm wide (critical dimension, must not be thinner than 0.6mm or thicker than 1.0mm to remain functional), one external lever trigger, and one moat catch tray (160mm outer diameter, 20mm deep, 90mm center cutout for the tower to sit in); FDM PLA or PETG (PETG preferred for the flexure part's fatigue life); minimum wall thickness 2.5mm on structural tower walls; internal baffle chute clearance 20mm minimum to pass a 16mm six-sided die without jamming; press-fit tower halves require 0.15mm total clearance at the alignment pins.

ideas.title: Cribbage Peg-Free Dial Scorekeeper Wheel
ideas.concept: A single-piece spinning dial scorekeeper that replaces the traditional cribbage peg board: a large numbered ring (0-121 track etched around the rim) with two rotating pointer arms per player, mounted on a low-profile base, so scores are tracked by rotating pointers instead of moving pegs that fall out and get lost.
ideas.rationale: Cribbage has seen a documented resurgence as a casual card/board hybrid among younger players via home-game-night content on TikTok and Instagram (hashtags like #cribbage and #cardgamenight trending in recent gift-guide and 'retro games are back' coverage), and lost pegs are the single most common complaint in cribbage board reviews on Amazon, indicating a specific unmet need.
ideas.differentiation: Every existing printed cribbage board on Printables/Thingiverse is a peg-hole board (a direct clone of the traditional design, inheriting the same lost-peg problem); this is a fundamentally different mechanism (rotating dial pointers, zero loose parts) aimed at travel and family use where lost pegs are the top complaint.
ideas.producibility_notes: 5 printed parts: base disc with printed track markings, 4 identical pointer arms (2 per player, distinct colors per player pair), 1 central axle boss printed into the base. No loose hardware; pointers snap onto the center boss with a 0.3mm clearance friction fit and are retained by a small printed detent bump so they don't spin loose during transport.
ideas.margin_case: Approx. 4hr print, ~140g PLA (~$4.20 material cost); sell at $22. Buyers already pay $20-35 for premium wooden cribbage boards; a novel no-lost-pieces mechanism justifies a comparable price for a lighter, cheaper-to-produce printed part.
ideas.prompt: Concept: A circular dial-based scorekeeping board for a card-counting game traditionally scored with pegs on a 121-point track. The board is a flat disc approximately 200mm diameter with a spiral numbered track (0 to 121, with clearly marked 5-point tick intervals) printed/engraved around two concentric spiral lanes (one lane per player), and 4 pointer arms (2 per player, one leading/one trailing marker per player as in traditional cribbage scoring) rotate around a central raised boss to indicate current score by their position along the spiral track. Purpose: a portable, peg-loss-proof scorekeeper for a classic two-to-four-player card game, aimed at families and travel/camping game sets where small loose pegs get lost. Style: retro game-night aesthetic, warm wood-tone or cream base with the two players' pointer arms in two contrasting bold colors (e.g., red and blue), clean engraved numerals, minimal decorative flourish beyond a thin rim border. Technical specification: overall diameter 200mm, thickness 10mm for the base disc; 5 parts total: 1 base disc with a central integrated cylindrical boss 12mm diameter x 8mm tall, and 4 pointer arms (each 70mm long, with a center hub bore 12.3mm diameter for a 0.3mm rotational clearance fit over the boss); FDM PLA material, single or dual color (dual color recommended: neutral base + colored pointers); engraved track numerals and tick marks must be at least 1.2mm deep to remain legible after printing (avoid features under 1mm); each pointer hub must include a small printed detent bump (0.5mm protrusion) that clicks past matching dimples on the boss every 30 degrees so pointers hold position and don't drift during handling; minimum wall/rib thickness 2mm.

ideas.title: Adaptive Angled Card Holder Rack for Limited-Mobility Players
ideas.concept: A tiered, angled card holder base that lets a player set standard-sized playing cards or board-game hand cards into a slotted rack in front of them, fanned and visible, without needing to grip and hold a hand of cards themselves.
ideas.rationale: Accessibility advocacy in tabletop gaming has grown into a recognized purchasing niche, evidenced by dedicated resources like the Meeple Like Us accessibility review project and Gen Con's ongoing Access-Ability programming, plus a steady stream of arthritis/limited-dexterity card-holder listings among Etsy's best-selling 'accessible games' category, indicating buyers (often gift-givers for elderly relatives) specifically search for and pay for this exact accommodation.
ideas.differentiation: Most printed card holders on Printables are simple single-slot semicircle stands; this is a two-tier angled rack (back row taller than front row) that fans a full hand of 10-15 cards clearly visible to the player and to no one else, sized generously for players with reduced fine-motor control, rather than optimized purely for compactness.
ideas.producibility_notes: 1 printed part, no assembly, no multi-color needed. Slot width is the single critical dimension (must comfortably fit 2 standard playing cards back to back, roughly 0.6mm combined, with clearance) and must be called out explicitly.
ideas.margin_case: Approx. 2.5hr print, ~70g PLA (~$2.10 material cost); sell at $16. Single-part, single-color, low-cost print, but sold at accessibility-market pricing (comparable widely-sold arthritis card holders run $10-20), giving strong margin for a genuinely simple object because the value is functional, not decorative.
ideas.prompt: Concept: A two-tier angled tabletop card holder rack that fans a hand of playing cards or board-game cards upright and visible without requiring the user to grip them. It has two parallel curved slotted rows, a shorter front row and a taller back row offset behind it, each row containing 12-15 narrow slots angled slightly outward in a fan pattern so cards inserted into both rows overlap visibly like a hand of cards held by another person. Purpose: an assistive accessory for board-game and card-game players with arthritis, limited hand strength, or other fine-motor impairments who cannot comfortably hold a fanned hand of cards, intended as a gift item for elderly or disabled family members. Style: simple, minimal, utilitarian rounded-corner design with no decorative ornamentation, single neutral color (e.g., matte black or wood-tone), smooth chamfered edges for safe handling. Technical specification: overall footprint approximately 250mm wide x 90mm deep x 60mm tall at the tallest point of the back row; single printed part, no assembly required; slot width 1.0mm (sized to snugly hold 1-2 standard 0.3mm-thick playing cards with slight friction) and slot depth 20mm; 13 slots per row spaced 18mm apart center-to-center following a gentle 300mm-radius arc for the natural fan appearance; base thickness 6mm minimum for stability so the rack doesn't tip when cards are inserted; FDM PLA material; no features under 1mm except the intentional 1.0mm card slots which must be printed accurately since they are the primary functional element.

ideas.title: Woodland Faction Meeple Set for Asymmetric Forest War Games
ideas.concept: A set of 4 distinct animal-shaped player-piece meeples (cat, bird, fox/vagabond, and a generic 4th 'expansion' silhouette slot) sized to match standard meeple bases, designed as an upgrade/replacement set for asymmetric woodland-themed war games that ship with plain cardboard tokens for some factions.
ideas.rationale: Root has remained a consistently top-100 ranked game on BoardGameGeek since release and is specifically known within the hobby for its imbalance between plastic/wood-quality components for some factions versus flat cardboard tokens for others, a frequently cited complaint in BGG forum threads and YouTube 'component upgrade' review videos, which is exactly the kind of gap that drives aftermarket meeple-upgrade purchases.
ideas.differentiation: Existing printed meeple sets on Printables tend to be generic humanoid pawns in solid colors; this set is theme-specific animal silhouettes (cat soldier, bird officer, fox rogue) sized as drop-in replacements for a named game's known cardboard-token weak point, targeting an identified and discussed community complaint rather than a generic aesthetic upgrade.
ideas.producibility_notes: 12 printed parts total (4 unique animal sculpts x 3 units each, single sculpt reused via multiples in a batch), single color per faction batch (4 separate color runs: e.g., orange/black/red/grey), no assembly, no sub-1mm features but fine detail on ears/tails requires a 0.2mm-nozzle-friendly minimum feature size of 1.5mm.
ideas.margin_case: Approx. 3hr print for a set of 12 pieces, ~60g PLA total (~$1.80 material cost); sell at $19 for the 12-piece set. Component-upgrade meeple sets for named asymmetric war games commonly sell for $15-25 per faction set on Etsy specifically because they solve a known, discussed component-quality complaint, supporting strong margin on a low-material print.
ideas.prompt: Concept: A set of 12 small stylized animal-shaped game piece tokens (3 each of 4 designs: a standing cat figure, a perched bird figure, a crouched fox figure, and a simple rabbit figure) each mounted on a circular base matching standard board-game meeple footprint dimensions. Purpose: a component-upgrade replacement set for asymmetric woodland-themed strategy board games that ship some player factions with plain flat cardboard tokens instead of sculpted pieces, aimed at hobbyists who want visual parity and tactile quality across all factions. Style: charming low-poly stylized animal silhouettes (not photorealistic), smooth simplified forms readable at small scale, each animal design printed as a single solid color per batch (suggested palette: orange cat, brown-grey bird, russet fox, tan rabbit), minimal fine surface detail beyond the recognizable silhouette. Technical specification: each piece approximately 22mm tall x 15mm base diameter; base thickness 3mm, base diameter matches a standard 15.5mm meeple footprint hole if used with existing meeple bags/trays; 4 unique sculpt files each printed x3 for a 12-piece set; single-color FDM PLA print per animal design (4 separate color runs, no multi-material printing required); minimum feature size 1.5mm on thin details like ears and tails to remain printable without support failure; no assembly; flat base with a slight 0.5mm chamfer for stable standing on a game board.

ideas.title: Mars Colony Production Tracker Wheel Set
ideas.concept: A set of 8 individual rotating production-tracker dials (one per resource type) that mount along the edge of an economic space-colonization board game's player board, replacing loose resource cubes with a spin-to-set numbered wheel for each resource's current production and stock level.
ideas.rationale: Terraforming Mars has remained continuously ranked in BGG's overall top-20 games for years and is one of the most frequently discussed titles in 'my resource cubes keep rolling off the table' complaint threads on r/boardgames, a specific and recurring pain point that directly motivates aftermarket resource-tracking accessory purchases.
ideas.differentiation: Existing Terraforming Mars accessories on Printables are mostly card-storage boxes; this targets the specific, frequently-complained-about mechanic (loose resource cubes sliding around the small player board tracks) with a purpose-built rotating dial replacement rather than another storage box.
ideas.producibility_notes: 16 printed parts (8 dial bases + 8 dial faces, one pair per resource), snap-fit assembly per dial (no hardware), each dial base includes an integrated retaining lip. Numerals on dial faces need to be at least 1mm deep to stay legible. Suggested single color per dial pair with contrasting engraved numerals (achievable via color-change filament swap or simple single-color if numerals are debossed rather than a second color).
ideas.margin_case: Approx. 6hr print, ~200g PLA (~$6.00 material ccost); sell at $32 for the 8-dial set. Buyers of this specific game are documented complainers about the exact problem this solves, and comparable printed 'production tracker' upgrades already circulate informally in the game's fan community at similar price points, supporting the ask.
ideas.prompt: Concept: A set of 8 small circular rotating dial trackers, each dial showing a numbered scale from -5 to 10 around its rim with a fixed pointer notch, designed to sit along the resource-production track edge of an economic space-colonization board game's player mat, replacing small cubes that are pushed along a printed track. Each dial is a two-part assembly: a base ring with an integrated center post and retaining lip, and a face disc that snap-fits over the post and rotates freely to select the current value. Purpose: a tabletop accessory that stops small resource-tracking cubes from being bumped and rolling off the table during play of a strategy board game with multiple resource-production tracks, for hobbyist players. Style: minimal sci-fi utilitarian aesthetic, flat matte finish, one distinct color per resource type (suggested: red, black/steel, blue, green, gold/yellow, brown, orange, silver-grey for the 8 resource types), debossed (recessed) numerals and tick marks rather than raised text for durability. Technical specification: each dial assembly 35mm outer diameter x 6mm thick when assembled; base ring includes a center post 8mm diameter x 5mm tall with a 0.5mm retaining lip at the tip; face disc has a matching center bore 8.3mm diameter for a 0.3mm rotational clearance snap-fit over the post and past the retaining lip; numeral/tick engravings debossed 1.0mm deep minimum for legibility; 8 unique base+face pairs (16 parts total) in FDM PLA, single color per pair (8 separate color runs), no external hardware, no glue required for assembly.

ideas.title: Magnetic Modular Deck Box System for TCG and Deckbuilder Games
ideas.concept: A deck storage box built from individually-printed 60-card-capacity modules that snap together side-by-side via embedded magnets, so a player can click 2-6 modules together into one carrying block sized to however many decks they're currently playing.
ideas.rationale: The trading-card and deckbuilder market has posted record recent sales figures (Pokemon TCG and Magic: The Gathering both reported record annual revenue in recent Hasbro/Wizards and Pokemon Company financial disclosures), and 'modular deck box' is a recurring highly-favorited search category on Etsy's TCG-accessory storefronts, showing sustained demand for exactly this storage format.
ideas.differentiation: Most printed deck boxes on Printables/Thingiverse are single fixed-capacity boxes; this system lets a buyer own just the number of modules they need and expand later, using embedded magnets (not printed snap-fit alone) for a satisfying strong click-together connection that fixed boxes and simple snap-fit competitors don't offer.
ideas.producibility_notes: Per module: 2 printed parts (box shell + slide lid) plus 4 small cylindrical neodymium magnets (5mm diameter x 2mm thick, press-fit into printed magnet pockets, sold as a hardware insert). Multi-module purchase means the customer just prints/orders more identical modules. Magnet pocket tolerance is the critical dimension (5.1mm diameter, 2.1mm depth for a firm press-fit) and must be explicit for the pipeline.
ideas.margin_case: Approx. 3hr print per module, ~90g PLA (~$2.70 material) plus ~$0.80 for 4 magnets = ~$3.50 cost per module; sell at $14 per module (customers typically buy 2-3 at once). Magnetic modular systems command a premium over plain boxes in the TCG accessory market specifically because of the expandability and satisfying connection, supporting margin even with the added magnet cost.
ideas.prompt: Concept: A single storage module sized to hold approximately 60 sleeved trading cards or deckbuilder game cards, consisting of a rectangular open-top box shell and a slide-in lid, with 4 cylindrical magnet pockets molded into each of the two narrow side faces so that multiple identical modules can be pressed together side-by-side and held firmly by magnetic attraction, forming one larger combined storage block. Purpose: modular, expandable card storage for trading-card-game and deckbuilder board-game players who want to store a variable number of decks as one connected unit rather than several loose boxes, for hobbyists who play multiple games or decks. Style: clean minimal geometric design with rounded edges, single solid color (suggested dark charcoal or deep navy) with a thin embossed line-art border on the lid face, no other ornamentation, utilitarian aesthetic aimed at looking neat on a shelf. Technical specification: module external footprint 95mm long x 70mm wide x 100mm tall; internal cavity sized 90mm x 65mm x 95mm to hold approximately 60 double-sleeved cards; 2 printed parts per module (box shell, slide lid that inserts into a 3mm rail groove on the shell's top edge); each of the 2 narrow side faces (70mm x 100mm) has 4 magnet pockets, 5.1mm diameter x 2.1mm deep, positioned in the same relative locations on every module (corners, 10mm inset from edges) so any two modules align and mate magnetically when pressed together; requires 4x cylindrical neodymium magnets 5mm diameter x 2mm thick as a purchased hardware insert, press-fit into the pockets (no glue needed if diameter tolerance is held to 0.1mm); FDM PLA or PETG material; minimum wall thickness 2mm; lid rail groove clearance 0.3mm for smooth sliding without rattling.

ideas.title: Twist-Lock Poker Chip Carousel Caddy
ideas.concept: A round, tiered caddy that holds 4 denominations of poker chips in stacked cylindrical wells arranged around a rotating turntable base, so the dealer spins the caddy to present the needed denomination to each player instead of passing chip trays around the table.
ideas.rationale: Home poker night has seen renewed post-pandemic popularity as a recurring social-gathering format, reflected in sustained strong sales of home poker sets on major retail marketplaces and a steady stream of 'poker night setup' content across YouTube and TikTok home-entertaining channels, indicating continued buyer interest in poker-hosting accessories.
ideas.differentiation: Existing printed poker chip holders on Printables are almost universally static stacking tubes or flat trays; this is a lazy-Susan-style rotating caddy specifically designed for a host to spin toward each player, a distinct table-service mechanic not addressed by static holders.
ideas.producibility_notes: 3 printed parts: base ring, rotating turntable top (with 4 integrated chip wells), and a low-friction center pivot boss printed into the base. No hardware; pivot uses a printed bearing-surface fit (0.3mm clearance) rather than a ball bearing to keep part count low.
ideas.margin_case: Approx. 6hr print, ~220g PLA (~$6.60 material cost); sell at $30. Dedicated poker accessories (chip trays, dealer buttons, carousels) commonly sell in the $25-40 range to home-poker hosts who already spent $50-150 on a chip set and are willing to add a hosting-experience upgrade.
ideas.prompt: Concept: A round rotating chip caddy for poker night consisting of a stationary outer base ring and a rotating inner turntable disc that spins freely on a central pivot, with 4 open-top cylindrical wells built into the turntable arranged in a cross pattern, each well sized to hold a stack of approximately 20 standard 39mm poker chips of one denomination. Purpose: a dealer's table accessory that lets a poker night host spin the caddy to present the correct chip denomination to whichever player needs it, instead of passing loose chip trays around, aimed at home poker-night hosts. Style: casino-inspired aesthetic with a felt-green and black color scheme (green turntable top, black base ring), subtle radial groove texturing on the base for a classic card-table look, moderate ornamentation limited to a thin gold-tone accent ring molded around the turntable's outer edge. Technical specification: overall assembled diameter 220mm, height 90mm; 3 parts total: base ring (220mm diameter x 20mm tall) with a central integrated pivot boss 30mm diameter x 15mm tall, turntable disc (200mm diameter x 15mm thick) with a center bore 30.3mm diameter for a 0.3mm rotational clearance fit over the pivot boss, and the 4 chip wells (each 42mm inner diameter x 70mm deep, walls 2.5mm thick) printed as part of the turntable disc in a cross layout; FDM PLA material, suggested 2-color print (green turntable, black base) though single-color is an acceptable fallback; pivot boss requires a smooth surface finish (print with boss vertical, no visible layer ridges greater than 0.1mm) to rotate without excessive friction; minimum wall thickness 2.5mm on chip well walls for structural rigidity when full.

ideas.title: Magnetic Snap-Base Miniature Flight Stands for Skirmish Wargames
ideas.concept: A set of 5 clear-styled flight-stand bases with a recessed magnet pocket on the bottom and a matching magnet pocket on top under the miniature peg, so painted miniatures can be popped on/off bases and bases can stick to a metal-lined carrying case for transport without loose miniatures rattling around.
ideas.rationale: Games Workshop has reported record consecutive years of revenue growth in its published financial results, and the broader skirmish-miniature wargaming hobby (Warhammer 40k, Age of Sigmar, and similar systems) has correspondingly driven strong demand for compatible aftermarket bases and transport solutions, a well-documented Etsy and Printables best-seller category.
ideas.differentiation: Most printed miniature bases on Printables are purely cosmetic (textured terrain bases) with no functional transport feature; this set focuses specifically on the magnetic pop-off/secure-transport mechanic, solving miniature damage and rattling during transport rather than just base aesthetics.
ideas.producibility_notes: 5 printed base parts (one shared design, ordered as a batch of 5), each requiring 2 small neodymium magnets (6mm diameter x 2mm thick) press-fit into printed pockets, one under the base and one under the integral peg socket. Magnet pocket tolerance (6.1mm diameter x 2.1mm depth) is the critical producibility dimension.
ideas.margin_case: Approx. 2.5hr print for a set of 5 bases, ~50g PLA (~$1.50 material) plus ~$3.00 for 10 magnets = ~$4.50 total cost; sell at $18 for the 5-pack. Magnetized base sets are an established $15-25 aftermarket category in the miniature wargaming hobby specifically because they prevent expensive painted-miniature damage, justifying the price over the low material cost.
ideas.prompt: Concept: A set of 5 identical round miniature display bases, each with a slightly textured cracked-earth top surface, a standard peg socket in the center sized for common plastic miniature peg tabs, and two magnet pockets: one recessed into the underside of the base itself, and one recessed into the base of the peg socket so a magnetized peg-adapter or magnetized miniature tab can click into place. Purpose: functional display and transport bases for painted plastic skirmish-wargame miniatures, letting hobbyists pop miniatures on and off bases and secure bases to a metal-sheet-lined carrying case without rattling or falling, for miniature wargaming hobbyists. Style: cracked-earth battlefield texture on the top surface (shallow irregular fissure pattern), matte grey or sand-tone single color, no paint included (buyer paints separately), minimal additional ornamentation beyond the terrain texture. Technical specification: 5 identical bases per set, each base 32mm diameter x 3mm thick (standard skirmish-game base size); center peg socket 5mm diameter x 4mm deep sized for common plastic miniature peg tabs; one magnet pocket 6.1mm diameter x 2.1mm deep centered on the base underside, and one magnet pocket 6.1mm diameter x 2.1mm deep at the bottom of the peg socket; requires 2x cylindrical neodymium magnets per base (10 total for the 5-pack), 6mm diameter x 2mm thick, press-fit as a purchased hardware insert; FDM PLA material, single color; top surface texture depth 0.5-1.0mm for the cracked-earth effect (must stay above 0.5mm to remain visible after printing); minimum base thickness 3mm to accommodate both the peg socket depth and magnet pocket without a weak point.
